summary: Sort up to 20 pictures or objects into two or more groups and count each group.
Answer questions about data shown in a T-chart, object graph or picture graph.
Recognize a penny, nickel, dime and quarter by sight.
Compare two objects directly using words like longer, shorter, taller, heavier, lighter.
Name and describe triangles, squares, rectangles, circles, cubes and spheres, including in the real world.
Tell where objects are using position words like above, below, beside, between, behind.
Read, write and show numerals 0 to 20 with objects.
Break teen numbers 11-19 into ten ones and some more ones using objects or drawings.
Count to 100 by ones and tens, and count back from 10 by ones.
Recognize how many objects (up to 10) are in a structured arrangement without counting.
Count up to 20 objects, write the number, and know rearranging does not change the count.
Given a number from 0 to 20, count out that many objects.
Compare two groups of up to 10 objects as more than, fewer than or the same.
Add and subtract within 5.
Find the number that makes 10 with a given number from 0 to 9, using objects or drawings.
Break numbers up to 10 into two parts in more than one way, using objects or drawings.
Solve joining, separating and part-whole story problems within 10.
Describe, extend and make simple repeating patterns (AB, AAB, ABB, ABC).
Sort pictures or objects into three or more groups of up to 10 each.
Ask a survey question, collect data in up to three categories, graph it and answer questions.
Put three objects in order by length by comparing them directly.
Estimate, then measure length using same-size nonstandard units with no gaps or overlaps.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Name coins and $1, $5, $10 bills and write their values with cent or dollar signs.
Find the total value of a set of all pennies, all nickels or all dimes, up to $1.
Sort a mix of polygons into groups and explain the sorting rule.
Describe attributes of named flat and solid shapes such as rhombus, hexagon, cone and cylinder.
Name flat and solid shapes found in everyday objects.
Tell whether a shape is flat (2D) or solid (3D) and explain why.
Compare two flat shapes or two solid shapes of different sizes and orientations using math words.
Read, write and show numbers to 100 with models, drawings, tens-and-ones words and expanded form.
Show that two-digit numbers are made of tens and ones and that place gives a digit its value.
Build and break apart numbers 1-99 into tens and ones in more than one way.
Find one more, one less, ten more and ten less than a number up to 99.
Count forward or back by ones from any number up to 120.
Skip count by 5s and 10s up to 100, starting at any multiple of five.
Compare two numbers up to 100 using the words greater than, less than or equal to.
Split squares, rectangles and circles into 2 or 4 equal parts and call them halves or fourths.
Decide whether an addition or subtraction equation within 10 is true, in varied formats.
Break numbers up to 20 into parts in different ways and write each as an equation.
Solve add-to, take-from and part-whole story problems within 20 with unknowns in all positions.
Add and subtract within 10 fluently.
Use the fact that order does not change a sum (commutative property) for sums to 20.
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation within 10.
Add a two-digit number and a one-digit number or a multiple of ten using place value.
Subtract multiples of ten from 10 to 90 and write the equation.
Make, describe and extend a growing shape pattern.
Make, describe and extend repeating patterns (AB, AAB, ABB, ABC) for three more terms.
Ask a survey question, collect data in up to four categories, and draw tally, picture, dot and bar graphs.
Choose a tool to estimate and measure length in inches, feet or yards.
Tell and write time to five minutes with a.m. and p.m.
Total a set of coins (to $1) or bills (to $100); write it with ¢ or $.
Name flat and solid shapes such as pentagons, octagons and rectangular prisms in everyday objects.
Sort figures into polygons and non-polygons and defend each choice.
Sort flat shapes into triangles and quadrilaterals and justify each choice.
Read, write and show numbers to 999 with models, number names and expanded form.
Show that three-digit numbers are made of hundreds, tens and ones.
Build and break apart numbers up to 999 into hundreds, tens and ones in several ways.
Find 10 more, 10 less, 100 more and 100 less than a three-digit number.
Count forward and back by ones, tens and hundreds within 999 and spot patterns.
Compare numbers up to 999 and record with words and the symbols >, =, <.
Tell which multiple of ten a two-digit number is closest to, as a step toward rounding.
Split squares, rectangles and circles into halves or fourths in different ways and name the parts.
Explain that more equal parts of the same shape means each part is smaller.
Add and subtract two-digit numbers within 100 with a strategy and justify the answer.
Decide whether an addition or subtraction equation within 20 is true, in varied formats.
Solve one-step add, subtract and compare story problems up to 99 with unknowns in any position.
For a number 0-99, find the number that adds to it to make 100.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently.
Group three addends in different ways to find a sum up to 20 (associative property).
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation within 20.
Pair up a set of up to 20 objects to tell whether the count is odd or even.
Write a repeated-addition equation for objects in equal groups or arrays (total up to 25).
Describe, extend and create growing shape patterns, up to three terms.
Make and extend number patterns with an add or subtract rule within 100.
Collect data and show it in tables, scaled picture or bar graphs, or dot plots with titles and labels.
Solve one-step problems using data in tables, scaled graphs or dot plots.
List the possible outcomes of a simple chance event like rolling a die.
Find the area of squares and rectangles by tiling with unit squares and counting.
Find the perimeter of triangles and quadrilaterals when side lengths are given.
Decide whether a real situation calls for area or perimeter.
Find the value of coins up to $5 and write it in dollars-and-cents decimal form.
Tell and write time to the minute with a.m. and p.m.
Add and subtract time intervals to find elapsed time to the nearest half hour.
Estimate and measure length to the nearest half inch and whole centimeter.
Choose the best customary or metric unit for measuring a liquid volume.
Describe and draw right, acute, obtuse and straight angles and find them in shapes.
Identify and draw points, lines, segments, rays, and intersecting, parallel and perpendicular lines.
Read, write and show whole numbers to 999,999 in several forms and on number lines.
Build and break apart four-digit numbers using thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
Compare two whole numbers up to 999,999 using place value and >, =, <.
Round whole numbers up to 1,000 to the nearest 10 or 100.
Understand a unit fraction as one of 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8 equal parts of a whole.
Show fractions 0 to 1 with objects, sets, areas and number lines; write in numbers and words.
Write whole numbers as fractions and spot fractions equal to whole numbers.
Build fractions up to 5 from unit fractions and write them as mixed numbers or fractions above 1.
Recognize equivalent fractions between 0 and 1 with denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, 8.
Compare two fractions with the same numerator or same denominator using >, =, <.
Add and subtract within 1,000 using a strategy.
Model multiplication and division facts with factors and divisors to 10 and write matching equations.
Multiply and divide within 100 (factors to 10) flexibly using related facts.
Find the unknown number in a multiplication or division situation in any position.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction story problems up to 1,000.
Find, make and extend add or subtract number patterns for the next three terms.
Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors from 1 to 10.
Collect data and show it in tables, scaled bar graphs or dot plots using wholes, halves and fourths.
Solve one-step problems with whole-number and fraction data from tables and graphs.
List possible outcomes of a simple event and call it certain, possible or impossible.
Use the rectangle perimeter formula, including finding a missing side length.
Use the rectangle area formula in real problems and label answers in square units.
Total a set of coins and bills to decide whether there is enough money for a purchase.
Find elapsed, start or end time for intervals within 60 minutes.
Measure length to the nearest quarter inch.
Measure weight in ounces, pounds, grams and kilograms to the nearest whole unit.
Convert customary length, weight and liquid volume units from larger to smaller.
Classify triangles by sides (isosceles, equilateral, scalene) and angles (acute, right, obtuse, equiangular).
Arrange quadrilaterals in a hierarchy based on shared properties.
Read and write whole numbers up to 999,999,999 in word, standard and expanded form.
Estimate sums, differences, products and quotients by rounding to check if answers are reasonable.
Order up to three whole numbers below 1,000,000 and record with < or >.
Write tenths and hundredths as fractions, in words, with models and as decimals.
Compare decimals to hundredths using benchmarks and models, recording with >, =, <.
Make equivalent fractions, including ones greater than 1, using models.
Compose and decompose fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators using models.
Show with models how a mixed number equals a fraction greater than 1 and back.
Compare fractions and mixed numbers with like or unlike denominators using benchmarks.
Add and subtract whole numbers up to 100,000 with a strategy and justify the result.
Multiply a one-digit number by multiples of 10 and 100 using place value.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two digits by two digits, by decomposing.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with or without remainders.
Add and subtract fractions with like denominators and check if the answer is reasonable.
Add and subtract tenths and hundredths, including mixed numbers, using fraction-decimal equivalence.
Multiply a whole number by a unit fraction using models or equations.
See a fraction as a sharing division: numerator divided into denominator equal parts.
List all factor pairs of a number from 1 to 50 and say whether it is prime or composite.
Describe and extend a number pattern that follows a rule, using input/output tables.
Solve multiplicative comparison problems and write equations with a variable.
Solve two-step story problems with all four operations; write an equation with a variable.
Find the range and mode of whole-number, fraction or decimal data sets.
Solve two-step problems with whole-number and fraction data in tables, line graphs, bar graphs or dot plots.
Read tables, bar graphs, dot plots, line graphs and circle graphs to predict or draw conclusions.
Write the probability of a simple event as 0, a fraction, or 1.
Find area and perimeter of shapes made of rectangles by splitting them into rectangles.
Estimate and measure the volume of a rectangular prism by filling it with unit cubes.
Convert between larger and smaller units in one system (length, weight, volume, time) to solve problems.
Estimate and measure length to the nearest eighth inch or millimeter.
Name the origin and axes, and plot and label ordered pairs (including from tables) in quadrant one.
Graph and interpret first-quadrant points to represent real and math situations.
Read, write and show numbers to 999 with decimals to thousandths in several forms.
Explain how a digit's value changes when it moves places left or right, including decimals.
Round decimals to thousandths to the nearest hundredth, tenth or whole number.
Use exponent patterns to explain multiplying and dividing by powers of 10.
Compare fractions and mixed numbers by rewriting them with a common denominator.
Multiply a two- or three-digit number by a two-digit number, including the standard algorithm.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit divisors, with or without remainders.
Add and subtract decimals to hundredths, including money and making change.
Multiply or divide a decimal less than 1 (hundredths) by a one-digit whole number.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with unlike denominators, including word problems.
Multiply a fraction by a fraction or by a whole number, including word problems.
Divide a whole number by a unit fraction and a unit fraction by a whole number.
Use the least common multiple to find a common denominator.
Use the greatest common factor of two numbers up to 50 to simplify a fraction.
Find the rule for a function table and write it as an expression.
Write a two-step story as an expression with parentheses and evaluate it.

state_code: # - 2025 SC College- and Career-Ready Mathematics Standards (approved Dec 12 2023; PDF "Emended July 2026"):
# - Corrective Edits to the 2025 SC CCR Mathematics Standards (July 2026; edits of June 2024, July 2025, July 2026 already in the emended PDF):
# - SCDE Mathematics Standards Crosswalk 2025 to 2015 (April 2024), used to spot grade shifts:
# - SCDE publishes no crosswalk to CCSS; every ccss/kind value here is a judgement against the CCSS K-5 text.
# - DPSR: Data, Probability, and Statistical Reasoning
# - MGSR: Measurement, Geometry, and Spatial Reasoning
# - PAFR: Patterns, Algebra, and Functional Reasoning
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS SC DROPPED (no indicator covers them)
# - K.CC.C.7 compare written numerals (K.NR.3 standard title mentions numerals, its only indicator compares object sets)
# - K.G.B.5 build/draw shapes, K.G.B.6 compose shapes (only in K.MGSR.2.1 insight), 1.G.A.2 compose shapes, 2.G.A.2 partition rectangle into rows/columns of squares
# - 1.OA.A.2 three-addend word problems, 1.OA.C.5 counting on as addition (process standard only)
# - 2.NBT.B.6 add up to four two-digit numbers; 2.NBT.B.7 add/subtract within 1000 (moved to grade 3, 3.PAFR.1.1)
# - 2.MD.A.2 measure with two units, 2.MD.A.4 how much longer, 2.MD.B.6 number-line diagram sums
# - 4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.6, 4.MD.C.7 angle concepts and protractor measuring (SC starts measuring angles in 6.MGSR.2.2)
# - 5.NF.B.5 multiplication as scaling; 5.MD.C.5 volume formulas and additive volume (formula in 6.MGSR.1.5)
# - Partly dropped: 3.MD.A.2 grams/kilograms (weight moved to 4.MGSR.2.4), 3.G.A.1 (now 4.MGSR.3.2), 4.NF.B.4 non-unit fractions x whole (5.PAFR.2.2),
#   4.MD.A.1 metric conversion (5.MGSR.2.1), 5.NBT.A.3b compare decimals to thousandths (no grade-5 indicator), 5.NBT.B.7 limited to whole x decimal under 1,
#   3.NBT.A.3 (moved to 4.PAFR.1.2), 5.NF.B.3 (moved to 4.PAFR.2.4), 5.G.B.3/5.G.B.4 (moved to 4.MGSR.3.2), 2.OA.A.1 two-step (one-step only), 1.MD.A.1 indirect comparison.
# - Patterns strand: K.PAFR.2.1, 1.PAFR.2.1-2.2, 2.PAFR.2.1-2.2 (repeating, growing shape and add/subtract number patterns).
# - Probability from grade 3: 3.DPSR.2.1, 4.DPSR.2.1, 5.DPSR.2.1 (outcomes; certain/possible/impossible; probability as 0, fraction, 1).
# - Subitizing (K.NR.2.2); make 100 (2.PAFR.1.4); range and mode (5.DPSR.1.1); GCF to simplify (5.PAFR.3.2); circle and line graphs (5.DPSR.1.3).
# - Money starts in K (coin names) with value counting in grade 1; place value to 999,999 in grade 3; numbers to 999,999,999 in grade 4.
# - Coins in K/1 and coin totals in grade 3 marked "moved" from 2.MD.C.8 (CCSS money appears only there and in 4.MD.A.2).
# - K.DPSR.1.2 graphs mapped to 1.MD.C.4 (moved); K.MD.B.3 has no graphs.
# - 1.MGSR.2.3-2.5 shape naming, 2D vs 3D, comparing shapes are CCSS kindergarten content (K.G), so "moved" down a year.
# - 3.NR.1.1-1.3 (numbers to 999,999 and 4-digit composition) marked moved from 4.NBT.A.2; CCSS grade 3 has no explicit place-value range.
# - 3.NR.2.4 (fractions up to 5, mixed numbers) mixes 3.NF.A.1/A.2 with 4.NF.B.3; kept "edited".
# - 4.MGSR.2.2 elapsed time: CCSS splits it between 3.MD.A.1 and 4.MD.A.2; kept "edited".
# - 5.MGSR.1.1 composite area/perimeter mapped to 3.MD.C.7/4.MD.A.3 (moved); the grade-5 overview mentions fractional side lengths (5.NF.B.4), the indicator does not.
# - 5.MGSR.2.2 (measure to 1/8 inch) and 5.DPSR.1.2/1.3 linked to 5.MD.B.2 loosely; line and circle graphs are not CCSS.
# - 5.PAFR.3.1 LCM is CCSS 6.NS.B.4 (outside K-5); linked to 5.NF.A.1 for its common-denominator use. 5.PAFR.3.2 GCF has no K-5 code, so "new".
# - 5.DPSR.1.1 range/mode corresponds to CCSS grade 6 statistics (6.SP), outside K-5, so "new".
# - 2.PAFR.2.2 number patterns with a rule resemble 4.OA.C.5 but are marked "new", not moved two grades down.
